overview: Memeware 7.3's Criticals is a three-mode ground-spoof module whose handlers are almost entirely dead code: the module registers the modes 'Ground Spoof', 'Packet' and 'Mineplex', but the packet handler only ever reacts to the names 'Mineplex', 'Cubecraft' and 'GroundSpoof' - isMode compares with equalsIgnoreCase, so 'Ground Spoof' never matches and 'Cubecraft' is not registered at all. Only the Mineplex branch is reachable: every second tick while standing on ground it flips the outgoing C03 onGround flag to false and, on position packets, injects a silent C04 lifted 1.02E-9 blocks. The unreachable GroundSpoof branch would lift the update Y by a swing-gated decaying 0.001, and the unreachable Cubecraft branch would trail each C02 attack with three C04s (0.1232225 / 1.0554E-9 / 0) at 320ms intervals.

sections.p: Two handlers split the work. The PacketOutEvent handler inspects every outgoing packet before it is written to the channel: the Mineplex branch mutates C03PacketPlayer instances in place and uses PacketUtil.sendPacketSilent - a direct NetworkManager.sendPacket call that bypasses the event bus - for the injected C04. The UpdateEvent handler (the GroundSpoof branch) edits the motion event's y and onGround fields while a swing is in progress, so the modified values flow into the client's next movement packet. A Timer built on System.nanoTime()/1000000 gates the Cubecraft branch at 320ms, and a groundSpoofDist double (0.001, decaying 1E-11 per use, reset when it drops below 0.0001) drives the GroundSpoof lift. onEnable and onDisable only reset groundSpoofDist. Of the three registered modes, only 'Mineplex' maps to a live handler branch; 'Packet' has no branch at all, and 'Ground Spoof' is unreachable because the handler tests 'GroundSpoof' without the space.

The only reachable offset is the Mineplex pair: on every even tick (ticksExisted % 2 == 0) while isCollidedVertically is true, every outgoing C03 has its onGround flag forced to false, and if that C03 is a C04 position or C06 pos/look packet, a silent C04 at y + 1.02E-9 with onGround false is written straight to the channel. 1.02E-9 is far below the 1.8 server's 0.03 minimum movement distance, so the coordinate is ignored and only the flag applies - the player claims airborne without moving. The dead Cubecraft branch would send, in order, C04 y + 0.1232225 off-ground, C04 y + 1.0554E-9 off-ground, then C04 y onGround true, gated by the 320ms crit timer. The dead GroundSpoof branch would raise the update y by groundSpoofDist - 0.001 decaying 1E-11 per swing until it resets from below 0.0001 - and claim off-ground for the duration of each swing.

The packet order differs from most packet-criticals. The Cubecraft branch hooks the C02PacketUseEntity out-event itself, so the three C04s it enqueues through addToSendQueue are written behind the C02 that is already being sent - the server processes the attack first and the lift afterwards, which is why the branch relies on the following packets to carry the airborne state. The Mineplex branch is attack-agnostic: it runs on every movement packet, so a KillAura attacking during the even-tick window sends its C02 while the server believes the player is 1.02E-9 blocks off the ground, and the odd-tick on-ground claims reset the server fall distance again. The GroundSpoof branch keys off isSwingInProgress, tying each decaying lift to an actual swing. The module never checks reach, attack delay beyond the dead Cubecraft timer, or the target's hurt time, and the Cubecraft branch's 320ms cadence means the injected lift can arrive long after the attack it was meant to serve.

files.label: Criticals.java (module logic)
files.explanation: The module is a mode string plus two handlers. The constructor (line 20) registers 'Ground Spoof', 'Packet' and 'Mineplex', but the PacketOutEvent handler (line 25) tests isMode('Mineplex'), isMode('Cubecraft') and isMode('GroundSpoof'), and Module.isMode does an equalsIgnoreCase comparison against the registered value - so the 'Ground Spoof' mode never enters the GroundSpoof branch and 'Cubecraft' is not a registered mode at all. Only the Mineplex branch (line 30) is live: on even ticks while isCollidedVertically it sets packet.onGround = false on every C03, and for C04/C06 position packets additionally injects a C04 at y + 1.02E-9, onGround false, via PacketUtil.sendPacketSilent (line 36) - a sub-min-move lift whose coordinate the server ignores while accepting the flag. The Cubecraft branch (line 41) is the only C02-aware path: on an ATTACK packet-out, if the 320ms Timer delay has elapsed, it addToSendQueue's C04 y + 0.1232225 (false), C04 y + 1.0554E-9 (false) and C04 y (true), so the lift trails the C02 in the same flush. The UpdateEvent handler (line 59) implements the GroundSpoof pattern - setY(y + groundSpoofDist), setGround(false), decay 1E-11 - but only under the unreachable 'GroundSpoof' name. onEnable/onDisable (lines 71-79) reset groundSpoofDist to 0.001.

files.label: PacketUtil.java (send paths)
files.explanation: The module's two send paths define its packet ordering. sendPacketSilent calls mc.getNetHandler().getNetworkManager().sendPacket(packet) directly, bypassing the client's send queue and the event bus, so the Mineplex branch's C04 at y + 1.02E-9 is written immediately while the C03 being processed is still in flight. sendPacket routes through mc.thePlayer.sendQueue.addToSendQueue, appending to the tail of the outgoing stream, which is how the Cubecraft branch's three C04s end up behind the C02 whose out-event triggered them. The same split exists in the Nekoware fork, whose PacketUtil is identical apart from the package name.

countering.label: Criticals (combat-side vertical check)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's Criticals check runs on every attack and compares Arc's physics-derived ground state against the vertical speed at the moment of the C02. data.isOnGround() comes from Arc's own MovingListener ground tracking, not the packet flag, and getVerticalSpeed() is the processed delta of the last move. The Mineplex mode attacks with the client claiming off-ground while Arc still reports onGround and a vertical speed near zero (the 1.02E-9 lift is below even the movement threshold Arc processes), and the latent Cubecraft mode's 0.1232225 lift is a vertical speed of 0.12 - both sit far below the 0.37 floor, so every attack is 'critical while onGround'. Because Arc's ground state is world-derived, the module's onGround=false flips change nothing on the server's side of the check.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (vertical movement envelope)
countering.explanation: SurvivalFly rebuilds the vertical envelope from the previous move's momentum via vDistRel (line 212) and accepts only a few named vertical behaviors: zero-y on ground, a real jump, a step-up, riptide. The latent Cubecraft lift of 0.1232225 from a standing position is none of these - yAllowedDistance stays 0 and yDistanceAboveLimit is 0.12, feeding the (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) + max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) * 100 violation (line 233) and its set-back. The Mineplex 1.02E-9 lifts and the GroundSpoof 0.001 decay are deliberately below the 0.03 minimum move the server even processes, so they are invisible to the envelope - that residue is covered by the combat-side vertical checks rather than the movement model.

countering.label: SmallHop (mini-jump detection)
countering.explanation: Hawk's SmallHop documents its own motivation: small jumps 'can be exploited to bypass other checks such as speed and criticals'. The latent Cubecraft hop is the textbook case: wasOnGround true, deltaY = 0.1232225 in (0, 0.4), prevDeltaY <= 0, no accepted knockback and no slime bounce, and AdjacentBlocks.onGroundReally at the destination is false because the feet sit 0.12 above the floor - punish and rubberband. The Mineplex 1.02E-9 lift and the GroundSpoof decay band (0.001 down to 0.0001) fall inside onGroundReally's 0.001 tolerance and are not flagged, which is exactly why those constants were chosen; the check still closes off the family's larger offsets.

countering.label: fight.Critical (critical-hit validation)
countering.explanation: NCP's fight.Critical validates the fall distance behind every crit. Its divergence rule - Math.abs(ncpFallDistance - mcFallDistance) > 1e-5 while the player is judged on-ground - catches the Cubecraft pattern whenever the injected C04s do reach the server before a later attack: NCP's own accounting (noFallFallDistance) says the player never left the ground, while the server-side fallDistance has ticked up from the off-ground claims, and NCP's ray trace still reports ground. And because the three C04s trail the C02 by queue order, an attack that lands before any lift arrives carries zero fall distance and simply does not crit - the module's own wire ordering is what defeats the pattern.
